procedural_history.originating_court: This case originated as a Writ Petition (Civil) No. 463 of 2012 directly in the Supreme Court of India under its original jurisdiction.
procedural_history.impugned_order: The document does not explicitly state that a specific order was challenged. However, I.A. NO. 13 OF 2014 was filed in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 463 of 2012, and the Supreme Court considered the second prayer made in the I.A., which sought the appointment of an SIT to investigate the abuse of authority by the CBI Director.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: There were no high court proceedings, as the case was filed directly in the Supreme Court.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court, after reviewing a report by Mr. M.L. Sharma, found a prima facie case for investigation into the abuse of authority by Mr. Ranjit Sinha and considered the request to appoint a Special Investigation Team (SIT).

issue.issue_text: Whether a Special Investigation Team should be appointed to investigate the abuse of authority committed by the then CBI Director in order to scuttle inquiries, investigations and prosecutions being carried out by the CBI in coal block allocation cases.

facts: Allegations were made that the then Director of the CBI, Sh. Ranjit Sinha, met with persons accused in the coal block allocation cases without the presence of the investigating team.
The Supreme Court appointed a committee headed by Mr. M.L. Sharma, a former Special Director of the CBI, to conduct a preliminary inquiry into these allegations.
The M.L. Sharma Committee submitted a report to the Court.
application: The Supreme Court reviewed the report filed by the M.L. Sharma Committee.
Based on the report, the Court concluded that a 'prima facie case has been made out for investigation into the abuse of authority' by Sh. Ranjit Sinha.
The Court considered appointing an outside body to investigate but decided against it, noting that there had been a 'change of guard in the CBI' (a new Director was in place).
The Court decided to 'repose our faith in the impartiality of the CBI' to conduct the investigation.
The Court ordered that the Special Investigation Team (SIT) would be led by the current Director of the CBI.

The Director was instructed to take assistance from two nominated CBI officers, take the Chief Vigilance Commissioner into confidence, and receive legal assistance from the Special Public Prosecutor in the coal block cases.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the plea and appointed a Special Investigation Team (SIT), to be headed by the current CBI Director, to investigate the prima facie case of abuse of authority by the former Director, Sh. Ranjit Sinha. The decision was based on the findings of a preliminary inquiry report submitted by a court-appointed committee.

arguments.issue_text: Whether a Special Investigation Team should be appointed to investigate the abuse of authority committed by the then CBI Director in order to scuttle inquiries, investigations and prosecutions being carried out by the CBI in coal block allocation cases.
appellant_arguments: The petitioner argued for the appointment of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the then CBI Director, Mr. Ranjit Sinha.
The basis for this prayer was the allegation that Mr. Sinha had abused his authority to scuttle inquiries, investigations, and prosecutions in the coal block allocation cases.
respondent_arguments: The text does not detail the specific arguments made by the respondent (Mr. Ranjit Sinha), but it notes that his counsel made submissions to the court, implying opposition to the petitioner's prayer for an investigation.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A prima facie case is sufficient to warrant an investigation into an abuse of authority.
obiter: A matter of considerable public importance should be taken up with due earnestness.
The court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the allegations or the contents of the report.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Upon a careful perusal of the detailed report submitted by Mr. M.L. Sharma, the court found that a prima facie case has been made out for an investigation into the abuse of authority by the then CBI Director, Mr. Ranjit Sinha. While the court expressed no opinion on the merits of the allegations themselves, it concluded that the contents of the report made it necessary to order an investigation as requested by the petitioner.
legal_tests_applied: Whether a prima facie case has been made out for investigation.
policy_considerations: The matter is of considerable public importance.
Since there has been a change of guard in the CBI, the court decided to repose its faith in the impartiality of the CBI itself to conduct the investigation, rather than appointing an outside body.
